label: Engaged in ferocious dialectical opposition over civilization, human nature, progress, and the 1755 Lisbon earthquake
description: Jean-Jacques Rousseau engaged in a direct critique of Voltaire (François-Marie Arouet)'s foundational principles, rejecting core axioms in favor of a dialectically opposed framework.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Voltaire (François-Marie Arouet)'s perspective to Jean-Jacques Rousseau's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Direct contemporaneous dialogue and pedagogical transmission during the Enlightenment & Social Contract era.

label: Voltaire's defense of free inquiry and critique of dogmatic superstition directly inspired Kant's 'What Is Enlightenment?'
description: Immanuel Kant was fundamentally influenced by Voltaire (François-Marie Arouet)'s central inquiries, which shaped the evolution of their philosophical worldview.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Voltaire (François-Marie Arouet)'s perspective to Immanuel Kant's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the Enlightenment & Social Contract across history into the German Idealism & Romanticism.
